definition.text: Herman Daly (1938–2022) was an American ecological economist, best known as a senior economist at the World Bank and for the idea of a steady-state economy.

facts.text: As Senior Economist in the World Bank's Environment Department he helped draft policy guidelines on sustainable development.
He co-founded the journal Ecological Economics and served as an associate editor.
His 1973 anthology Toward a Steady-State Economy gathered writers such as Georgescu-Roegen, Boulding and Hardin, and was revised in 1980 and 1993.
In 1989 he and John B. Cobb proposed the Index of Sustainable Economic Welfare as a better measure of progress than GDP.
He is widely credited with originating the idea of uneconomic growth, though some credit Marilyn Waring.
He drew on his professor Nicholas Georgescu-Roegen's view linking the economy to the entropy law.
In 1996 he received the Right Livelihood Award for defining a path of ecological economics joining ethics, quality of life, environment and community.

definition.text: John V. Krutilla (1922–2003) was an American environmental economist who invented the concept of existence value, the economic value of undisturbed wilderness.

facts.text: He introduced existence value, the value of an amenity such as wilderness or a species simply existing, in his essay "Conservation Reconsidered".
He has been described as creating or stimulating most of the agenda of modern environmental economics.
He worked at Resources for the Future until retiring in 1988, and shared the first Volvo Environment Prize with Allen V. Kneese in 1990.

definition.text: Kate Raworth (born 1970) is an English economist known for doughnut economics, a model balancing essential human needs against planetary boundaries.

facts.text: She first set out the doughnut idea in a 2012 paper and expanded it in her 2017 book Doughnut Economics.
She criticises the principle of unlimited growth as destroying planetary resources while serving human needs poorly.
Her model aims to give everyone basic needs such as food and education without limiting future generations' opportunities.
She worked on the UN Human Development Report and spent over a decade as a senior researcher at Oxfam.

definition.text: Kenneth Boulding (1910–1993) was an English-born American economist, educator, peace activist and interdisciplinary thinker.

facts.text: His 1966 essay "The Economics of the Coming Spaceship Earth" argued that the economy must fit itself to an ecological system with limited resources.
He suggested treating Earth's ecosystem as a stock of assets.
He stressed that economic behaviour is embedded in a larger interconnected system and promoted an evolutionary rather than equilibrium approach to economics.
